what_worked: Accessible plain-language framing, honest caveats slide, and clear long-tail distribution chart with useful annotations.
fix_next: The $13.5M MRR figure is wrong (actual 30-day revenue ~$15.6M); several category revenue figures also appear fabricated—verify every number against the dataset.
verdict: Well-structured and readable but too many wrong numbers undermine trust.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '$13.5M combined MRR' — actual 30-day revenue is $15.6M; conflating MRR with 30-day revenue and getting the number wrong. Slide 5: AI at 31% of category revenue — actual share is ~31% of categorized revenue but the denominator is unclear and the chart axis label is missing units. Slide 6: AI '$1.81M combined monthly revenue' — actual AI total revenue is $2.36M. Slide 7: SaaS $588.7K vs actual $703.5K; Marketing $444.5K vs actual $1.317M; E-commerce $395.7K vs actual $1.112M; Analytics $357.8K vs actual $368.2K — Marketing and E-commerce are dramatically wrong. Slide 12: '$0' bucket shows 197 but dataset has 216 zero-revenue startups; median MRR $282 is unverifiable but plausible only if using a different field. Slide 13: B2B/B2C percentages computed on 712 non-missing rows but presented as if whole dataset — denominator not disclosed.

evidence.insight: Observations stay at the descriptive level: 'AI is biggest,' 'US leads,' 'long tail.' The Stan spotlight (slide 9) and social-following-vs-revenue point (slide 15) are the closest to genuine insight but remain surface-level. No median-vs-mean analysis, no B2B revenue premium, no anonymity revenue share.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: market overview → segments → leaders → distribution → geography → business model → opportunities → advice → caveats. Coherent sequence with a thesis ('winner-take-most indie economy'). Weakened by the generic advice slide (17) and the 'why this market exists' slide (14) which are opinion, not data.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets context well for a lay audience. Slide 19 caveats are honest about missingness and snapshot nature. Scope is clear. However, calling it 'MRR' when the dataset field is 30-day revenue is a framing error that propagates throughout.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple revenue figures are materially wrong: total revenue off by ~$2M, Marketing revenue off by 3×, E-commerce off by 3×. Zero-revenue count wrong (197 vs 216). The deck never distinguishes MRR from 30-day revenue. The $133.8M and $334M figures (slide 3) cannot be verified from the frozen dataset reference and appear fabricated.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark/light theme, good use of whitespace, legible typography, appropriate bar charts with annotations. Pie chart on slide 13 is acceptable. Histogram on slide 12 is well-designed. Some visual sameness across card-based layouts. No chart is misleading in design, though underlying numbers are wrong.
evidence.ai_slop: Slide 14 ('Why this market exists right now') is generic thought-leadership filler not grounded in data. Slide 17 ('Could you build one of these yourself?') is motivational advice unconnected to analysis — classic AI-generated padding. The consulting-style card layouts repeat across many slides.
